The commentary opens the surah with this oath before turning to the account of the People of the Trench: "By the sky with its mansions of stars (al-Buruj)!" The word "buruj" here may mean either the great celestial bodies, as though they were the mighty fortresses of the heavens, as the Qur'an says in Surah al-Dhariyat: ﴿And the heaven We constructed with power, and indeed We are its expanders﴾ (51:47). And in Surah al-Nazi'at it says: ﴿Are you the more difficult to create, or the heaven He constructed?﴾ (79:27).

Or "buruj" may mean the stations through which these celestial bodies travel, that is, when these bodies revolve within their orbit and cannot deviate from it by even a hair's breadth. The word "buruj" also points to their vastness, and the intention here is to cast the shadow of vastness over the atmosphere of this surah.

By the Promised Day. This is the day on which the decisions regarding the deeds and events of the world will be made. In this world, whoever has earned something will receive its reward or punishment. This day is called al-Yawm al-Mawʿud (the Promised Day) because Allah promised its coming: that after the reckoning, reward and punishment will take place on that day. Until that day, Allah granted respite to those who were wronged in the world and to those who wronged others. It will be a great day, which people await so that they may see what decisions are made within it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 85, verse 3:

﴿And of the witness and the witnessed.﴾ On that day the deeds of people will also be presented, and all people will also be presented, so all of them will be witnessed, and when all people see, they will also become witnesses. On that day everything will come out from behind the veil and will be visible to everyone.

This vast sky with its mighty celestial bodies, and this great day on which reckoning and accounting will take place, and in which all witnesses and witnessed ones will be gathered, the atmosphere created by their mention is, in its grandeur, its significance and its great assembly, suitable for the narration of the great tragedy of the People of the Trench (Ashab al-Ukhdud) within it. This wide and expansive atmosphere has, as it were, been created for the narration of this event and to give this truth weight, namely the atmosphere of the Resurrection, which is wider than the expanses of this world, and whose life and whose time are wider than the limited life and limited time of this world.

After preparing this atmosphere and clearing this wide field, the great event is now only briefly alluded to.

After this, the commentary explains what the trenches (al-ukhdud) are: they are a blazing fire. In fact, they dug pits in the earth, lit fire in them and filled them with fire, and in this way the pits were made into a blazing fire. That is, those pits were filled with a blazing fire.

"Cursed be the people of the trenches" (﴿قُتِلَ أَصْحَابُ الْأُخْدُودِ﴾). They deserve to be killed and burned in this manner, because when they committed this oppression, what circumstances were they in?

The passage begins mid-verse: "(They were) sitting by the pit, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers" (85:6-7 ff.).

Translation:

"Fire, kindled, containing fuel, when they were sitting around it, and they were witnessing what they were doing to the believers." This is a depiction through which their position and their situation are clearly revealed. These people are kindling a fire, seizing the believing men and women and throwing them into it, and sitting at the edge watching them burn. They are looking closely at the act of this hard-hearted person, observing the methods of punishment, and as the fire consumes their bodies, they rejoice and fix this painful scene upon their witnessing.

The believers were innocent. There was no retribution (qisas) against them that could be held over these oppressors.

وما نفقموا .................................... شھید (9:85)

﴿They had no grievance against them except that they believed in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is Witness over all things.﴾ (9:85)

The only reason for their enmity towards these believers was that they had believed in God, the Mighty and Praiseworthy in His own right, the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and that God sees everything.

Their only crime was that they believed in God, who is Mighty and Dominant, who is capable of whatever He wills, and who is al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), meaning that He deserves praise and thanks in every state and is Praiseworthy in Himself, even if ignorant and unwise people do not praise Him. He is worthy that people should believe in Him and worship Him alone, and the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. He sees everything and is present and watchful over all things. He also sees this particular event that befell the believers, that they were thrown into the trench. Through this statement of faith and through God's testimony, every believer who is tormented by rebellious and tyrannical people solely because of his faith finds consolation. God is a Witness, and He is sufficient as a Witness.

In short, this story is concluded in these brief verses. However, the act and the brutality of these people are so cruel and merciless that the heart of every reader is filled with hatred and revulsion towards them, and a person begins to think about what the effects and consequences of this event will be in the sight of God, what the significance of this event will be before God, and what kind of wrath these oppressors have become deserving of before God. The event has been narrated concisely, but in human thought this event has not ended here. Its effects and its reckoning before God remain.

This story has ended, yet the human heart is awed by this great achievement: that faith triumphs over a severe trial and that conviction takes precedence over life. There are people who disregard all the worldly interests and bodily desires. For these people, one path was also to abandon faith and take the provisions of life and depart, but how losing a bargain that would have been; in this way the whole of humanity would have, as it were, been defeated. They would have killed the lofty human values. Then life devoid of ideology would no longer appear worthless to people, they would have been content with slavery, and people would have become so degraded that after physical slavery they would also accept spiritual slavery. But these were great values, which they considered a profitable bargain to buy even while they were alive on earth, and which they preferred even while their bodies were burning. Thus these spiritual values triumph, and they emerge purified from the furnace of fire. After this, there is a reward with the Lord for them, and their enemies too will be reckoned with; so it is said.

What happened on this earth does not end here, with the thing that was to happen simply having happened and its effects also ending here. Its effects remain. Every deed has a requital and a recompense, and the event is not complete until that recompense takes place. So the outcome of the treatment these tyrants meted out to the believers is yet to come. And Allah is the One who will judge on the Day of Resurrection.

Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and women ﴿persecuted the believing men and believing women﴾, and then did not repent. They continued to advance in their misguidance, and no remorse overtook them.

﴿Then they did not repent; for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of burning﴾. Here the Qur'an has explicitly mentioned ḥarīq (burning). The meaning is the same as the punishment of Hell, but the word ḥarīq has been brought so that, in contrast with the punishment given to the People of the Trench (Aṣḥāb al-Ukhdūd), the word "burning" also appears here, since the word ḥarīq had been used for the punishment of the believers. However, there is a great difference between the burning of this world and the burning of the Hereafter, and between their intensity and their duration. In this world the fire that burns is kindled by human beings, whereas the fire of the Hereafter has been prepared by Allah. The fire of this world burns for a few moments and then goes out, but in the fire of the Hereafter they will burn for endless ages. In the burning of this world there is hidden the pleasure of Allah and the triumph of noble values, but when they burn in the Hereafter, they will be under Allah's everlasting punishment and wrath, and abasement, degradation and condemnation will accompany them.

As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in Paradise, and in it the bounties of Allah will be made available to them, and Allah will be pleased with them.

Those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. This is the true salvation and success.

﴿That is the great triumph.﴾ (11:85) The word fawz means salvation and success. To be saved from the punishment of the Hereafter is itself the great triumph, and gardens beneath which rivers flow are triumph upon triumph. With this outcome in the Hereafter, the account now reaches its completion, and this is the true conclusion and end for both parties. The events that occur on earth are only a part of the true events; they are not the whole story. The first commentary that follows this account is meant to establish in the hearts of the believers the reality that events do not end in this world alone. At the time this surah was revealed, a handful of Muslims in Makkah al-Mukarramah were enduring such hardships, and likewise, in every time and place in the world, those who work for Islam and suffer persecution are also meant to be told that the outcome of these acts of mischief will become apparent on the Day of Resurrection.

Here the seizing of God is called severe for this reason: the punishment that these rebels gave to the believers in the event under discussion was, in their own view, a severe punishment. It was also considered severe by people, but here it is said that the true seizing is the seizing of Allah, the Almighty and Subduer, the King of the heavens and the earth. What would be the punishment of those who hold a limited authority over a single piece of the earth, who are themselves weak and contemptible, and whose authority is also for a limited time?

It is worth noting here that the word (Rabbika), "your Lord," has been used to express the relationship between the Speaker, the Lord (ta'ala), and the addressee, Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ). This is your Lord, to whose lordship you are attributed, and in whose help and support you place your trust. And when the wicked and sinful people are persecuting the believers, in such circumstances the relationship with Allah is the most important provision.

Fundamentally, the concept of the origination and return of life is specifically associated with the beginning of life and, after death, with the second life in the Resurrection. But in every moment of night and day, the process of the beginning of life and the return of life continues without interruption. At every moment, the process of the origination of life and the creation of life is ongoing. Allah has established a system through which the continuity of life is maintained. Whatever comes into being is repeated, and this universe continually receives new life. Within this continuous system of origination and return, the event of the People of the Trench (Ashab al-Ukhdud) also passed by with its consequences. Allah had decreed it thus; it happened, and such events will continue to happen. Whether this event was an origination that will be repeated, or a repetition of earlier events of this kind, in any case in this world events have a beginning and also recur, and all of this takes place in accordance with Allah's Book of Decree (kitab al-taqdir).

Here the connection of forgiveness (maghfirah) is with the preceding verse.

﴿Then they did not repent﴾ (85:10). This is the boundless mercy of Allah and His great grace. It is an open door, and it is open to every one who returns and every one who repents, even if his sin and his disobedience are extremely grave. The word Wadud (the Most Loving) relates to the believers who have given their Lord precedence over everything. This is the station of love and the station of intimacy, which only the special servants of Allah can reach. Allah elevates to this station only those servants who love Allah in such a way that they give Him precedence over everything, over the most beloved of things. The quality of these servants is beyond the power of the human pen, unless Allah gives strength to some pen. This exalted station, to which these special servants are raised, is the station of Allah's love and true friendship. Friendship between the Lord and the servant! And the station of love from Allah towards His beloved and close ones! Therefore, compared with this rank and station, the life of this world has no worth, for it was bound to end in any case, and compared with this rank and station, the burning punishment also has no worth, for it was in any case for a limited time. These sacrifices are not even equal to a single moment of Allah's love and friendship.

Those people on this earth who are the slaves of a single person: if that temporal master says even one word in their praise, and if they see that because of some action of theirs joy has appeared on the face of that temporal master, the slave is nonetheless a slave, and that temporal master too is a servant and slave of Allah. But the special servants of Allah, whom Allah loves, whom the Mighty Lord loves, and who is the Owner of the Throne, who is High and Exalted, and who is Generous, if such a servant's life departs, it is nothing; if torment is inflicted upon them, it is nothing. Even if torment continues throughout the entire life of this world, that moment of love is worth sacrificing everything for, the moment of love from the Lord, the Most Loving, who is the Owner of the Throne and is Great.

﴿The Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ (85:15).

﴿The Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ (85:15).

This is the attribute of Allah that continually manifests itself at all times; it remains constantly in operation. Allah is the Doer of whatever He wills. His will is unrestricted: He chooses whatever He wishes, and does whatever He desires. And this attribute is lasting and everlasting; it is an attribute of Allah.

Sometimes Allah wills that victory be granted to the believers in this very world, and there is a wisdom in this. Sometimes it happens that faith is given precedence over punishment. Mortal bodies do pass away, but faith remains, and there is wisdom in this too. Sometimes He seizes the tyrants in His grip, and there is wisdom in this; and sometimes He similarly grants respite to other tyrants, and there is wisdom in this too. All His affairs are based on wisdom in accordance with His decree.

These are the wisdoms of Allah. The People of the Trench (ashab al-ukhdud) destroyed the believers, and they were given respite; and Pharaoh and Thamud were destroyed by Allah. All these events occurred in accordance with His absolute will, His wisdom and His decree. And the unrestricted will of Allah thus operates in this entire universe in accordance with wisdom. And Allah does whatever He wills. Here is one example of this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 85, verses 17–18:

This is a reference to two long stories, so the accounts of Pharaoh and the people of Thamud were known to the addressees. The Qur'an has repeated both stories many times. They are called "hosts" (junud) here because they were very powerful. The meaning is: do you know what their story was and what your Lord did to them? Allah does whatever He wills.

The stories of Pharaoh and Thamud differed in their nature and their outcomes. Allah drowned Pharaoh along with his host and delivered the Children of Israel. They were given dominion over the earth for a period, so that through them Allah might manifest His decree and fulfil His purposes. As for Thamud, Allah destroyed them, and a small number was saved along with Prophet Salih (peace be upon him); but after that, this small number was not given dominion over the earth. What happened was only that they were delivered from those wicked people.

These two events were a model of Allah's absolute will and His unrestricted purpose. They were also two examples for the Islamic call, and one of two outcomes may follow for it. Yes, there is also a third possibility, which befell the People of the Trench (Ashab al-Ukhdud). These events were being related to the small Islamic movement working in Makkah, to show that one of these events may befall the call to Allah. The picture was being shown not only to the Muslims working in Makkah, but also to the generations to come.

Finally, two decisive blows are struck upon the veil of feeling, and in both there is a decisive matter, which is the final judgement.

Majeed means exalted, worthy of honour, and of profound and genuine origin; to whom else can these attributes apply other than the Word of Allah? This Qur'an is in the Preserved Tablet (Lawh Mahfuz). We do not know what the nature of the Preserved Tablet is, because it is an unseen matter. Only Allah knows its reality. We can only grasp the impression that this expression leaves upon the mind, and the indications that the heart accepts, and these indications are that the Qur'an is a preserved book, and that in every matter its judgment is the final judgment. All things may come to an end, but this remains preserved. This point has been stated in the context of the story of the Ukhdud (the people of the trench), but the Qur'an's judgment is the final judgment in all matters.
